title: Frittata
subtitle: Italian open omelette baked in the oven
excerpt: Eggs beaten with cheese, started on the hob, then finished under the grill or in the oven until just set. Loaded with courgette, pepper, and spring onion. Eaten warm or cold, straight from the pan.

recipe.sourceNotes: The frittata is Italy's equivalent of the Spanish tortilla and French omelette: eggs cooked with a filling in a pan, but unlike the folded French omelette, the frittata is flat. The word comes from the Italian for fried. Unlike a Spanish tortilla, the frittata is finished under a grill or in the oven rather than being flipped. It can be eaten hot or at room temperature and keeps well in the fridge for two days, making it ideal for packed lunches.

content.text: The pan must be oven-proof with no plastic handle. Start the frittata on the hob to set the base, then transfer to the grill or a hot oven to set the top without needing to flip it. The frittata is done when the top is just set and not wobbly: the centre will continue to firm up as it cools.
Heat the grill to high. Beat the eggs with the Parmesan, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a 26 cm oven-proof frying pan over medium heat. Fry the courgette and pepper for 5 minutes until just softened. Add the spring onion and cook for 1 minute.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables. Tilt the pan to distribute evenly. Cook on the hob over medium-low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the base is set and the sides are pulling away from the pan.

Place under the hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the top is just set and lightly golden. Leave to cool for 5 minutes before sliding onto a board. Slice into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.
